sanskrit_verse:
कामक्रोधाभियुक्तार्त भयव्यसनपीडिताः।
रागद्वेषपरीताश् च ज्ञेयास् त्वप्रकृतिं गताः॥
transliteration: kāmakrodhābhiyuktārta bhayavyasanapīḍitāḥ | rāgadveṣaparītāś ca jñeyās tvaprakṛtiṃ gatāḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: Those overwhelmed by desire and anger, distressed by fear and addiction, and possessed by attachment and hatred—are to be known as having fallen from their natural state of consciousness.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority originates in consciousness stability, not emotional turbulence.
Causation stems from inner disorder manifesting as outer distortion.
Capacity-based responsibility is diminished in proportion to consciousness deviation.
Restoration logic demands re-alignment with innate nature prior to disturbance.
Consciousness alignment determines eligibility for participation in dharmic society.
executable_legal_axioms: IF SUBJECT exhibits kāma/krodha dominance THEN assign temporary guardianship of action to a stabilized witness.
IF SUBJECT demonstrates vyasana-induced incapacity THEN initiate detoxification and reintegration protocol before legal engagement.
IF RĀGA/DVEṢA overrides cognitive clarity THEN defer judicial capacity until equilibrium is restored.
IF AFFECTIVE STATE ≠ PRAKṚTI THEN trigger automatic nyāya-based restoration sequence.
IF CONSCIOUSNESS DEVIATION IS DETECTED THEN invoke aparokṣa śuddhi mechanism immediately.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Adjudication, any party demonstrating signs of consciousness instability—manifested through excessive desire, rage, fear, or addiction—is subject to mandatory psycho-spiritual stabilization prior to case involvement. The court must recognize that unstable consciousness distorts pramāṇa and invalidates legal agency. Authority lies only with those established in śuddha prakṛti.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Nyāya operates through sequential manifestation: desire/anger → loss of self-governance → distortion of perception → erroneous action. Responsibility is proportional to consciousness retention. Therefore, intervention focuses on reversing the causal chain through purification rather than imposing punitive consequences.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate aparokṣa śuddhi (direct purification) under qualified guidance.
Assign completion process for unresolved emotional bindings.
Reintegrate individual into community through witnessed dharma practice.
Restore cognitive clarity via śama-dama protocols.
Verify return to prakṛti through trika-based assessment tools.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law restores consciousness as the sole arbiter of justice. No punishment arises where understanding prevails. Reality aligns when beings abide in their original nature. Dharma is executed; existence affirms its integrity.
